off.name: patch
off.description:
Use the `patch` tool to edit files. Your patch language is a stripped‑down, file‑oriented diff format designed to be easy to parse and safe to apply. You can think of it as a high‑level envelope:

*** Begin Patch
[ one or more file sections ]
*** End Patch

Within that envelope, you get a sequence of file operations.
You MUST include a header to specify the action you are taking.
Each operation starts with one of three headers:

*** Add File: <path> - create a new file. Every following line is a + line (the initial contents).
*** Delete File: <path> - remove an existing file. Nothing follows.
*** Update File: <path> - patch an existing file in place (optionally with a rename).

Example patch:

```
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: hello.txt
+Hello world
*** Update File: src/app.py
*** Move to: src/main.py
@@ def greet():
-print("Hi")
+print("Hello, world!")
*** Delete File: obsolete.txt
*** End Patch
```

It is important to remember:

- You must include a header with your intended action (Add/Delete/Update)
- You must prefix new lines with `+` even when creating a new file

patchText.description: The full patch text describing add, update, and delete operations

freeform.grammar:
start: begin_patch hunk+ end_patch
begin_patch: "*** Begin Patch" LF
end_patch: "*** End Patch" LF?

hunk: add_hunk | delete_hunk | update_hunk
add_hunk: "*** Add File: " filename LF add_line+
delete_hunk: "*** Delete File: " filename LF
update_hunk: "*** Update File: " filename LF change_move? change?

filename: /(.+)/
add_line: "+" /(.*)/ LF -> line

change_move: "*** Move to: " filename LF
change: (change_context | change_line)+ eof_line?
change_context: ("@@" | "@@ " /(.+)/) LF
change_line: ("+" | "-" | " ") /(.*)/ LF
eof_line: "*** End of File" LF

%import common.LF

off.name: edit
off.description: Edit the contents of a file by finding and replacing exact text. When editing text from Read output, preserve the exact indentation (tabs or spaces) and omit the line-number prefix, such as `1: `. Never include the prefix in oldString or newString. Write line breaks as \n; the file's existing CRLF or LF line endings are matched and preserved. To change line endings themselves, make oldString and newString differ only in \r; that edit applies to the exact bytes. If there is no exact match, the edit retries while ignoring typographic quote, dash, and space variants, then trailing whitespace on each line. The edit fails if oldString is not found. By default, oldString must identify a UNIQUE location. Multiple matches FAIL unless replaceAll is true. Add more surrounding context to disambiguate, or set replaceAll to true to replace every occurrence. Use replaceAll when the change should apply to every occurrence, such as renaming a variable.

oldString.description: Exact text to find and replace

newString.description: Text to replace oldString with (must differ from oldString)

replaceAll.description: Whether to replace every occurrence of oldString. When false, oldString must match exactly once. Defaults to false.

off.name: glob
off.description: Search file paths using a glob pattern (examples: "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.tsx").

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files against

path.description: Directory to search. Defaults to the current working directory.

hidden.description: Include hidden files and directories (default: false).

limit.description: Maximum number of matching files to return (default: 100)

off.name: grep
off.description: Search file contents using ripgrep's regular expression syntax or literal text matching. Use it to locate specific code, symbols, or text patterns, and narrow searches with `path` or `include`. Returns matching file paths, line numbers, and line previews.

pattern.description: Regular expression or literal text to match in file contents.

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the current working directory.

include.description: Glob pattern to filter files (for example, "*.js" or "*.{ts,tsx}")

literal.description: Treat `pattern` as exact text instead of a regular expression (default: false).

limit.description: Maximum number of matching lines to return (default: 100)

off.name: read
off.description: Read the contents of a file or directory. Supports text files, images, and PDFs. Each text line is prefixed by its 1-based line number as <line>: <content>. The prefix is for reference and is not part of the file content. Directory entries are returned one per line. Use offset and limit to read large files or directories in sections. Prefer one larger read over many small slices, and use grep to find specific content in large files.

offset.description: The line or directory entry to start reading from (1-based)

limit.description: The maximum number of lines or directory entries to read (defaults to and capped at 2000)

next.description: The line to continue reading from. Absent when the content reaches the end of the file.
The entry to continue reading from. Absent when the listing reaches the last entry.

off.name: skill
off.description:
Load a specialized skill's instructions and resources into the current conversation when the task at hand matches its description.

The skill ID must match an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user.

id.description: The ID of an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user

off.name: write
off.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

Missing parent directories are created automatically.

Use this tool to create new files or overwrite existing files. For partial changes, use the edit tool instead.

path.description: Path to the file to write to

content.description: Content to write to the file

codemode.description: Apply multi-file edits inside `*** Begin Patch` ... `*** End Patch`. Start each operation with `*** Add File: <path>` (every content line prefixed with `+`), `*** Delete File: <path>`, or `*** Update File: <path>` (optional `*** Move to: <path>`, then `@@ [context]` hunks with space/`-`/`+` line prefixes).
